s1.syndrome_frame: chronic, painless, periocular swelling with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
persistent mass despite antibiotics for presumed postoperative cellulitis
granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis on histopathology
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
several-month history of periocular swelling
history of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
left levator resection for ptosis
dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
mass persisted despite two courses of antibiotics
non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim on examination
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid
no evidence of malignancy on histopathology
bacterial and fungal stains were negative

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and periocular involvement are consistent with sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showing granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and mucin is consistent with IgG4-related disease

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Periocular swelling and granulomatous inflammation without evidence of malignancy or infection are consistent with idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and mucin is consistent with necrobiotic xanthogranuloma

shortlist.label: Foreign body granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: History of recent surgery and presence of granulomatous inflammation suggest possible foreign body reaction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below her left lower eyelid, with granulomatous inflammation on histopathology and no evidence of malignancy or infection, is most consistent with idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease. The lack of systemic symptoms or other organ involvement also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: No mention of systemic symptoms or other organ involvement typical of sarcoidosis

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: No elevated IgG4 levels mentioned and histopathology does not specifically support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: Typically associated with paraproteinemia and has distinct histopathological features not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Foreign body granuloma
rejected.why: No history of trauma or foreign body exposure, and histopathology does not suggest a foreign body reaction
